steps.name: Saria
steps.text: A most remarkable speech, Mr. Vice President.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: People were moved to tears, even in the Rhine lounge.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: I didn't think I would move the most eccentric, most maverick scientists of Columbia.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: But I've received enough flowers, banners, strongly worded letters of support, and soldier figures painted in my likeness over the last few hours.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Not from Rhine.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: ...For the better, I suppose. Let's get back to the topic at hand.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: How should we define that 'tree' floating in the sky, from a scientific perspective?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: If you really want to know the scientific principles behind it, I could spend the whole afternoon explaining how its roots will spread across the land, and its branches and leaves across the sky.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: From a scientific perspective, however, all you need to know is that when it is fully grown, it will be able to collect energy and information from across Columbia and process it centrally.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: You mean... an energy well like the S.H.A.F.T., but on a national scale?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: And a server, too. Bidirectional, to boot.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: The roots and branches go both ways—not only from the ground to the sky, but also from the sky to the ground.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Haha.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: No need to force yourself to understand these things. You can zone out the way you did when you visited our Trimounts headquarters.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: It was your words that saved the tree when dozens of guns from the Department of Defense and hundreds of cameras from Maylander media were pointed at it.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Miss Wilson's words truly tugged at the heartstrings. Even an old man like me couldn't help but think back to the wild days of youth.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I see.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: And there I was, thinking that it was because you didn't want to give away the chance to define this tree to Maylander or the Department of Defense.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: An exhibition, a speech, Sky Fever and patriotism have made you the overwhelming darling of public opinion over the other candidates, in the span of just a few hours.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: But have you thought about the future you would need to paint, in order to not let your supporters down?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Or was it always your plan to improvise your speech?

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: You know about the understanding between Kristen and the Department of Defense. Kristen would build Arc-01, and it was none of Rhine's business who the DOD used it against.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Since I already have the authority to define this tree, I don't suppose it would have broken through the Starpod before everyone's eyes, if I didn't discuss with Rhine when defining it?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Of course you don't have to discuss with anyone, be it Nasti, myself, the generals, the lawmakers, or that plushie on your shoulder.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: ...Hehe.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: I take back what I said about you when I was chatting with my secretary.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: You're easier to deal with than Kristen.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: State your demands.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Lift the lockdown on Propeller Paradise and allow the escaped plate to return to the capital's route for repairs. As to those involved in the incident...

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: 'Escaped'? That's not how D.C. will define what has happened.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Researchers who stand on the front lines of Columbian science would never flee in the face of foreign sabotage, would they?

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: What else?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Lift the lockdown on Rhine Lab... you know what I'm talking about.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: You and I should hold an official meeting as soon as possible. You can't ask the government to undo something we haven't done. We've only ever been curious...

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: What can Rhine Lab do?

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Seriously, is no one sleeping tonight? I should have held some night wilderness tours.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: Heh. You just wouldn't stay still, would you, even when the plate's broken down.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: I could say the same about you. You look like a clerk gazing blankly at the sky outside after coming back from vacation.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: Well... I was scared, but also excited, when we started fighting the Maylander people.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: You almost scared ME when you tried to bite that agent's finger off.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: I'm not really an emotional guy. The last time I was so excited was when I got approved for that Sky Loan.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: The loan shark was showing off levitating devices at the entrance to the local bar. There were so many people watching that they broke the fence.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: In the end, it wasn't education or economic circumstances that decided who got the loan, but who could fly a drone the highest and furthest.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Which was how you ended up being the sucker who got scammed into it.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: That night, I stupidly bragged to my wife, showing off the finger I used to move the control stick and win a chance for the future...

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: It was only a few days later that you realized there was no battery in the controller at all.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: Yeah, I should never trust myself when blood gets into my head.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: But you still charged the blockade with us without a second thought, didn't you?

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: Yeah. Now we're like cystybeasts to the slaughter in the wilderness, waiting for the government to decide our future...

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: I feel like an onion thrown into a washing machine, getting layers after layers peeled off in these tides of fevers...

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Do you want to escape the washing machine, or do you want to be more than a powerless onion?

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: A few years ago, I had an idea while going into the Bleached Wasteland for the third time.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: If I sneaked inside with a truckload of pure gold ore, and took it through the border checkpoint in broad daylight...

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Columbians would forget all the terrifying legends in the blink of an eye and begin another Great Expansion, and it wouldn't be much different from what we're going through.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Even if it began with a bored tour guide rather than a scientist who split the sky; even if it was a hoax rather than a milestone.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: We always try to see new possibilities inside the door marked 'impossible', to escape the laws of common sense that seem to have no end, to go somewhere else and live a different life.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: You, me, the hundreds of Propeller Paradise testers, even that Rhine researcher assistant, Sky... we're all the same.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: The onion can't get out of the washing machine...

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: But we can remember why we chose to go inside.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: If the government doesn't hang us all for treason tonight, I want to stay on Propeller Paradise, run Lucky Cystybeast, and pay my debts.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: Can you deliver a letter to my wife? I don't really trust regular Messengers.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Would you like to join Ferne's Tours? I could deliver YOU.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I don't believe it. There can't be a single scientist on Terra like you.

steps.name: Scientific Consultant?
steps.text: (Sound of hammering)

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: How did you meet Gustave? Did you know about his and Maylander's plan?

steps.name: Scientific Consultant?
steps.text: (Sound of metal being polished)

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Shame I never actually got to teach him a lesson. The old fox ran off with Maylander's people after the levitation layer fell.

steps.name: Scientific Consultant?
steps.text: He was taken away in handcuffs.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Handcuffs? Ha! He wanted me to take the fall for Propeller Paradise, but he's the one who ends up going down!

steps.name: Scientific Consultant?
steps.text: (Sound of metal clanging)

steps.name: Scientific Consultant?
steps.text: Good.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: You've been sitting here the whole day with those pliers and hammers... what are you studying?

steps.name: Scientific Consultant?
steps.text: I'm preparing for a journey.
The Kuranta gestures to the bottom of his 'shoes'. Only then does Gordon realize that the sound that the Kuranta makes when walking does not come from shoes.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: A piece of crescent-shaped metal... nailed to your feet? Doesn't it hurt?

steps.name: Scientific Consultant?
steps.text: No. Feet are more trustworthy than shoes in treacherous terrain, such as the swamps of Sargon, the icefields of Sami, and the barrenlands of Columbia.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: So you don't plan on hiding your identity from me.

steps.name: Scientific Consultant?
steps.text: My role is insignificant in this entire event.

steps.name: Scientific Consultant?
steps.text: I simply came to help a friend, and made a new friend along the way.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I do so hate free spirits.

steps.name: Scientific Consultant?
steps.text: You have enough experience to be my travel companion. But you won't do it.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: ATAO's gonna be purged after this accident. Why should I not go back when the old fox no longer has any influence?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Besides, you recognized everything in my collection room. I'll always be inferior to you if I traveled with you.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I'll make good use of all ATAO resources available to me. You won't recognize Five-Four the next time you see it.

steps.name: Scientific Consultant?
steps.text: I look forward to it.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Is there any place you haven't been? Like beyond the Starpod, I guess?

steps.name: Scientific Consultant?
steps.text: There are many paths that no one has trodden before.

steps.name: Scientific Consultant?
steps.text: If there indeed comes a day when humanity stands among the clouds, I will continue to cast my gaze to the land.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: I saw you coming this time, Mercia.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: It's rare to see you not burying your head in work. Are you waiting for someone?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: What about you? Your colleagues already pulled out of Propeller Paradise, before the sun had set.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Another rule of secretaries? You have to be the last one to leave?

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: Just ran into a bit of trouble when packing.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: (Speaks in Sarkaz) Hover.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: Oh, thank you. I was wondering how I would get them down there.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Yet you chose the most scenic route, one that would take you around the tree.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: I wanted to see the final resting place of Væla... your mother.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Her epitaph is the leaves that grow upon it.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Look up on your way out. She might have the wind carry one to you, if she still remembers you.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: You're not angry that I used Væla to complete Maylander's mission?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: You also defied Maylander's orders in order to help her.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: If it's to prison that you go from here, I would not consider it a shining example of Columbian justice.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: No need to worry about that.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: The Tin Man once decorated himself with drone parts that Mr. Selene discarded. Usefulness is not the only standard that he uses to judge.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: And this little rebellion won't be, either.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Mm.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: Ah... I think that's the one you were waiting for?

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: I'll take my leave, then.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Give me the parameters, Sky.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: Transmission complete. Nothing out of the ordinary. The tree is in great shape.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: But you already know that, don't you?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Just making sure the battle didn't wreck your brain.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: The first thing I learned on the streets of Trimounts was how to fight. I wouldn't be here at Rhine if a fight or two could wreck my brain.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Until I come back, you're in charge of the tree's regular maintenance, any derivative projects, and all our staff, workers and testers in Propeller Paradise.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: I need you on top of your game.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: I got the projects, but the workers and testers... they have been asking what you liked. They wanted to give you a token of their appreciation before you leave.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: They stayed because of you, Director Lunorey.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: What did you tell them?

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: Uh... I don't know. I have no idea what you like... other than our work.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Take a Starpod Wars stamp to Pitt tomorrow. He'll tell you everyone's personality and interests.

spans.text: stamp to Pitt tomorrow. He'll tell you everyone's personality and interests.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: Director...

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: The first thing I learned on the barrenlands was how to deal with people.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: What do you like, then?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: It's not hard to find out.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: It's time to go. I'll leave the tree in your hands.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: Huh? What about the one you were waiting for?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: He's used to traveling alone. He's probably already left.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: Left? But we're in the barrenlands!

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: He'll find a way.

steps.name: Rhine Lab Researcher
steps.text: Hey, stop. This is Rhine Lab HQ. Visitors need to register over there.

steps.name: Rhine Lab Researcher
steps.text: I noticed you the moment you walked in. Hard not to, given the clatter you make when walking. Did you just come back from the barrenlands or something? At least change your clothes, if you want to steal company secrets.

steps.name: Rhine Lab Researcher
steps.text: What the... director-level access? Who are you?

steps.name: Rhine Lab Researcher
steps.text: I-I'm sorry. I'll take you upstairs now. The others are waiting for you in the conference room.
Thank you.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: ...That's the gist of it. The rest of the details are on the slide.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Propeller Paradise has docked with Max, D.C.. The District will now proceed to perform repairs and take inventory.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Hundreds of tech firms, more than a thousand research projects on the sky and flight, and some twenty to thirty-thousand people... it could take months to complete.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Fortunately, Saria's negotiation with Jackson was a success, and the Rhine Engineering Section will be able to focus on their work at Propeller Paradise.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Sky Jagger is in charge until I get back. He's matured a lot.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Wow, you're actually developing the new guys.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Good work, Nasti.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Thanks for your help... I would thank you even more if you deleted the photos where you make faces with my appearance.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Nah, don't think so.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Say, aren't you gonna tell me about your mom?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Something's different about you... not sure what, exactly, but in a good way.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Nasti...

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Alright. I cried, I came to terms with a few things, and strengthened my resolve with a few things. That's all.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Ahem. I didn't leave my lab to watch your little tête-à-tête.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: You've been a little too committed to science lately, Ferdinand. I'm almost starting to miss the days when you were scheming left and right to take over the company.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: And why do you think I'm not doing that?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: I'll ask you to recall that it was MY breakthroughs in high-energy physics that have kept all our sections afloat these past two years, ladies!

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Yes, sure, thank you for your help.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I'm guessing Dorothy didn't come to the meeting because she didn't want to hear you gloat.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Hmph. She went back to Site 359 right after the inquiry. She said she had a few dreams... girl never looks forward.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Saria. Nasti's already sent the experiment results concerning the 'tree' to my mailbox. We're not here only to discuss the Propeller Paradise matter, are we?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Of course not.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Then who are we waiting for?
Perhaps you might be interested in seeing data from the Infy Icefield?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: You're back, Maryam. Finally.

steps.name: Maryam
steps.text: Sorry, it's been a long time since I've been in Columbia. Took me some time to fit my hoof-irons. Broke them in on the walk from D.C. to Trimounts.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: I'm glad I didn't wait for you on Propeller Paradise. I had a car that could have taken both of us back to Rhine together.

steps.name: Maryam
steps.text: ...You know, I never considered that at all.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Someone obsessed with searching for death in every corner of Terra would be used to working alone. I figured.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: It takes two people with director-level access to activate the core unit of that tree. I had wondered who Saria sent to help Nasti...

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: The legend is already a pile of bones in the wilderness. The media questions if the director of Rhine's Scientific Investigation Section even exists. There's definitely no better choice, but—

steps.name: Maryam
steps.text: You want to know who arranged it? Justin Jr.

steps.name: Maryam
steps.text: He had some investments in Čappat, and no sooner had I left the Infy Icefield than he got in touch.

steps.name: Maryam
steps.text: He told me to go to Columbia, and straight to D.C.. I got Gustave's invitation soon after... Justin Jr. had obviously, let's just say, pulled a few strings.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Then why did you—

steps.name: Maryam
steps.text: Why did I come back to Rhine? I found a fragment of that spherical superstructure in the depths of the Infy Icefield, where the rootless flowers bloomed the brightest.

steps.name: Maryam
steps.text: You guessed it? Yes, it's the structure that Kristen's files mentioned. She said people in the old times called it the Stargate.

steps.name: Maryam
steps.text: I'm sure Saria will share the information with you soon. Any more questions, Ferdinand? I thought not.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Haha. Nothing's changed about how you ask and answer your own questions, Maryam. You've left Ferdinand with nothing left to say.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Alright, looks like everyone's here.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: This meeting is rather overdue. For the past two years, all of mainstream Columbian media and the tech tabloids have made the same judgment...

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: 'The gap where Galleria Stellaria disappeared is a scar upon the Starpod, and a scar upon Rhine.' They've even come up with a whole narrative on the cancellation of Rhine's end-of-year cocktail party.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: We were all busy, that's all.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Yes, but now we finally have some time.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: The joint project between Engineering and Ecological had some unexpected twists and turns, but the final result was a smashing success. Nasti, you're now holding the key to a brand new domain.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: ...If we can keep it in our hands.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Maryam's discovery in the Infy Icefield has proven beyond all doubt that those strange tales that Kristen collected are, indeed, based on actual fact.

steps.name: Maryam
steps.text: Perhaps it will help us rebuild dialogue with the old era.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: And Muelsyse has brought back data from our observation station in Kjerag...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Data that's very interesting... or very dangerous.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I'm sure you've heard about the events in Bolívar. Twenty science teams have gone missing in the Black Flow.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Explorers and schemers will be excited if there are any developments with that swamp. Rhine should act too, Saria.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Magallan is already on her way.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: The events and phenomena that have unfolded since Kristen's incident indicate that the most well-hidden secrets of Terra all lead to the same answer.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: It will tell us the reason for Terra's existence, and whether it is a disaster or a brave new 'world' waiting for us in the future.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Rhine Lab has already made preparations, but that alone is not enough. We must respond to the fear of the unknown, and go boldly where no one has gone before...

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: What you said was absolutely correct, Nasti.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: However, Rhine Lab must be the one to turn that key.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: (Mutters) Whoa...

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Of course, we'll have a make-up cocktail party.
What's this, Justin Jr.?

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: A newspaper sample. I would like you to think of a title for this article here before it goes to print. Are these scientists gathered to 'Mourn the End of Sky Fever'...?

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Or preparing to 'Usher in a Tide of New Changes?'
You sent a screenshot of your communications with your colleagues to the The Savior?

spans.text: You sent a screenshot of your communications with your colleagues to the

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: More appropriate to put it as a DOD-aligned newspaper getting its hands on certain documents that could not be obtained by official means.
But I heard your Control has already reached an understanding with Jackson concerning Propeller Paradise.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: None too thrilled about it, are you? But it won't stop me from making another deal with you.

You understand that, in the aftermath of the Horizon Arc Project, Rhine Lab's credibility with the Department of Defense has become roughly the equivalent of Mama John's scratch-off lottery tickets—garbage.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Which is why I only came to you after Saria reached an understanding with Jackson.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: In the aftermath of the setback in Bolívar, the failure of the Horizon Arc Project, and the Propeller Paradise incident, the Department of Defense's credibility with President Mark Max has become...

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Well, I suppose I should spare you the proverbs.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: I don't know what exactly our scientists are planning, but I know the value they can create. In this, I'm sure we're in agreement.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: I'm a businessman, and my priority is Rhine's business interests.
Sounds like I have no reason to refuse.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: It's a pleasure doing business with you.
To be frank with you, I didn't think much of you when Blake recommended you...

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Hah. I'm sure you remember my life story that I just shared, which is a fairly interesting one, if I do say so myself...

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: All you need to do is think something of fate. As for your attitude toward the one who controls its pulse—

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: That's rarely in your hands.
